question: The iceberg phenomenon of disease refers to the fact that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. most cases of a disease remain undetected in the community and only a small proportion come to medical attention

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Like an iceberg, only the visible tip of a disease is clinically apparent while the larger submerged portion stays hidden in the community

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — diseases occur only in cold climates: Climate is unrelated to the concept, which was borrowed from fishing

C — diseases affect only elderly persons: Age does not define the phenomenon

D — every case of a disease is reported to the health authority: If every case were reported there would be no hidden portion

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because so many cases stay hidden, community surveys find far more disease than clinic attendance figures suggest
option_1: most cases of a disease remain undetected in the community and only a small proportion come to medical attention
option_4: every case of a disease is reported to the health authority

question: A community nurse finds that several cases of typhoid in a village have all occurred in families that draw drinking water from the same open well. In the epidemiological triad the open well is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. environment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A contaminated water source is an environmental factor that brings the agent into contact with the susceptible host

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — host: The host is the person who becomes infected

B — vector: A vector is a living carrier such as a mosquito and is not involved in typhoid

C — agent: The agent is the organism that causes the disease, here Salmonella typhi

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Correcting the water source prevents further cases far more effectively than treating the cases alone

question: Which of the following is a host factor in the epidemiological triad?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the age, immunity and nutritional status of the person

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Host factors are the characteristics of the person such as age, sex, immunity, nutrition and genetic make-up that influence susceptibility

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the quality of the drinking water: Water quality belongs to the environment

C — the virulence of the organism: Virulence is a property of the agent

D — the temperature and rainfall of the area: Climate is an environmental factor

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Improving nutrition and completing immunisation raises host resistance, which is why growth monitoring and immunisation are linked programmes
option_1: the age, immunity and nutritional status of the person
option_4: the temperature and rainfall of the area

question: A disease that is constantly present in a community at a low but steady level is described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. endemic

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An endemic disease is habitually present in a community at an expected, steady level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — epidemic: An epidemic is the occurrence of cases in clear excess of the expected number

C — sporadic: Sporadic cases occur occasionally and irregularly without a steady pattern

D — pandemic: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across countries and continents

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The expected level of an endemic disease is the baseline against which an outbreak is detected

question: Transmission of infection through a mosquito is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. vector borne indirect transmission

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mosquito is a living carrier that transmits the organism from one host to another, which is indirect vector borne transmission

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — airborne transmission: Airborne transmission occurs through droplet nuclei suspended in air

B — transmission by a fomite: A fomite is an inanimate object that carries infection

D — direct transmission: Direct transmission is person to person without an intermediate carrier

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Vector control therefore interrupts transmission at the point where the parasite leaves one host for the next

question: The main purpose of the National Health Mission is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. strengthen the health system so that affordable and quality care reaches the poorest households

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mission works to make the public health system deliver accessible, affordable and accountable care, with special attention to the poor and to women and children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — provide only curative care in medical colleges: It covers primary, secondary and tertiary care and not medical colleges alone

B — replace all state health departments: It supports and does not replace the state health systems

D — run only immunisation camps: Immunisation is only one of its many components

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Most of the flexible funds that pay for village level nursing posts and for outreach camps come from this mission
option_1: provide only curative care in medical colleges
option_3: strengthen the health system so that affordable and quality care reaches the poorest households

question: In the rural public health system, the first point where a qualified doctor provides curative care is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. primary health centre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The primary health centre is the first contact point where a medical officer provides curative and preventive services to the community

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — sub-centre: The sub-centre is staffed by an auxiliary nurse midwife and a male health worker and has no doctor

C — community health centre: The community health centre provides specialist services at the referral level

D — district hospital: The district hospital provides the highest level of care within the district

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient who bypasses the primary health centre burdens the referral centres, which is why outreach services are strengthened

question: Under the norms of the National Health Mission, one sub-centre in a plains area usually serves a population of about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 5000

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In the plains a sub-centre is expected to cover about five thousand people, while in hilly, tribal and difficult areas the norm is about three thousand

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 3000: Three thousand is the norm for hilly and tribal areas rather than for the plains

B — 30,000: Thirty thousand is the norm for a community health centre

C — 20,000: Twenty thousand is the population norm for a primary health centre in the plains

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The norms tell the nurse whether her population load is unusually heavy, which is evidence to ask for additional staff

question: Under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme, the key element of the strategy for a newly diagnosed sputum positive patient is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. ensure free drugs with directly observed treatment and follow up every dose and every report

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Free drugs with direct observation of treatment and systematic follow-up are the core of the programme, because incomplete treatment produces resistance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — admit every patient to hospital for two months: Hospital admission is needed only for very sick patients

B — give treatment only if the patient can pay: Treatment is free, and charging the patient defeats the whole programme

D — prescribe the drugs on the first visit and leave the patient to collect them himself: Leaving a poor patient to buy drugs is the commonest reason for default

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the sputum at the end of the intensive phase, as a positive report means the treatment must be reviewed
option_1: admit every patient to hospital for two months
option_2: give treatment only if the patient can pay
option_3: ensure free drugs with directly observed treatment and follow up every dose and every report
option_4: prescribe the drugs on the first visit and leave the patient to collect them himself

question: The main preventive activity of the National AIDS Control Programme at the community level is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. promote awareness, condom use, safe blood and testing with confidentiality

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme combines awareness, prevention of transmission through sexual contact and blood, and confidential testing with treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stop all testing to reduce fear: Stopping testing hides the epidemic and prevents people from getting treatment

B — isolate all infected persons: Isolation is unnecessary, since the virus is not spread by casual contact

D — vaccinate the whole population: No effective vaccine is in routine use

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Confidential counselling and testing must always be offered together, and the result is never disclosed without the person's consent
option_3: promote awareness, condom use, safe blood and testing with confidentiality

question: The cold chain is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a system of people, equipment and procedures that keeps vaccines at the correct temperature from the factory to the child

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The cold chain is the whole system, including trained people, that maintains the potency of vaccines at every step from manufacture to administration

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the list of vaccines needed for a year: A vaccine list is a stock record and not the cold chain

C — a chain of refrigerators kept in a hospital: Refrigerators are only one component of the system

D — a device for transporting blood only: The cold chain covers vaccines and other temperature sensitive products, not blood alone

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A break anywhere in the chain, even for a short time, can make a whole batch of vaccine useless without any visible change
option_1: the list of vaccines needed for a year
option_2: a system of people, equipment and procedures that keeps vaccines at the correct temperature from the factory to the child
option_3: a chain of refrigerators kept in a hospital

question: Most routine vaccines in the cold chain must be stored at:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. plus 2 to plus 8 degrees Celsius

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Routine vaccines are kept between plus two and plus eight degrees Celsius in the main store and the ice lined refrigerator

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 0 degrees Celsius exactly: A temperature near freezing damages the freeze sensitive vaccines

C — minus 20 degrees Celsius: A temperature of minus twenty degrees Celsius is used for certain vaccines and for storing ice packs

D — room temperature of about 30 degrees Celsius: Room temperature destroys potency within hours or days

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The temperature is read and recorded twice a day, and any excursion is reported at once and the potency of the stock reviewed

question: While preparing for an outreach immunisation session the nurse notices that the vaccine vial monitor on a vial of oral polio vaccine has turned to the discard point and the expiry date has not yet passed. She should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. discard the vial at once and record it, because the monitor shows that the vaccine has been exposed to too much heat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The vaccine vial monitor darkens with cumulative heat exposure, and at the discard point the potency can no longer be assured whatever the expiry date says

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — use the vial only for older children: The vial must not be used for any child

B — put the vial in the freezer overnight and use it the next day: Freezing does not restore a heat damaged vaccine and destroys some vaccines outright

C — use the vial as it is still within the expiry date: The expiry date does not reveal the heat exposure that the monitor detects

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Discarded vials are recorded in the stock register and returned to the store, as the loss has to be accounted for
option_1: use the vial only for older children
option_2: put the vial in the freezer overnight and use it the next day
option_3: use the vial as it is still within the expiry date
option_4: discard the vial at once and record it, because the monitor shows that the vaccine has been exposed to too much heat

question: Which vaccine must never be allowed to freeze?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. hepatitis B vaccine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hepatitis B vaccine and other vaccines containing an aluminium adjuvant are damaged by freezing and must be kept between plus two and plus eight degrees Celsius

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — BCG vaccine: BCG is also a freeze dried vaccine

B — measles vaccine: Measles vaccine is a freeze dried vaccine and tolerates freezing

C — oral polio vaccine: Oral polio vaccine may be stored frozen for long term use

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Freeze sensitive vaccines are kept away from the evaporator plate and never in the freezer compartment

question: A community health centre in the rural health system is designed mainly to provide:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. referral services with four to six specialist beds and surgical facilities

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The community health centre offers specialist consultation and inpatient care, including surgical and obstetric facilities, and acts as a referral centre for primary health centres

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only immunisation and family planning services: Also preventive services, but they are not its main purpose

B — only outpatient care by an auxiliary nurse midwife: An auxiliary nurse midwife works at the sub-centre and not at this level

D — care exclusively for tuberculosis patients: Tuberculosis care is part of a programme and not of only one centre

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Knowing which services each level provides prevents unnecessary referral and saves the patient time and money
option_2: only outpatient care by an auxiliary nurse midwife
option_3: referral services with four to six specialist beds and surgical facilities

question: A 24-year-old woman living below the poverty line in a village delivers a baby at home with the help of a trained birth attendant. Under the Janani Suraksha Yojana the nurse's responsibility is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. help the family to register the birth, complete the paperwork, arrange the first immunisation and follow up the mother and baby at home

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scheme supports the mother with cash assistance and with continued care, so post natal home visits, registration and starting immunisation are the nurse's tasks

🔍 Key Clues: 24-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give the cash benefit without any follow-up: Handing over the money without follow-up loses the health purpose of the scheme

B — advise her to have the next delivery at home as well: Institutional delivery for future pregnancies is actively promoted

D — refuse any benefit because she did not deliver in a hospital: A home delivery attended by a trained birth attendant still qualifies for the benefit

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The scheme also pays the accredited social health activist, which is one reason a village worker closely follows every pregnancy
option_1: give the cash benefit without any follow-up
option_2: advise her to have the next delivery at home as well
option_3: help the family to register the birth, complete the paperwork, arrange the first immunisation and follow up the mother and baby at home
option_4: refuse any benefit because she did not deliver in a hospital

question: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke mainly works through:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. screening, health promotion and management of non-communicable diseases at the primary level

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme screens people above thirty years, promotes a healthy lifestyle and manages hypertension and diabetes at the primary level with proper referral

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — immunisation of adults: Immunisation does not prevent these diseases

B — treatment of only cancer patients: The programme covers several non-communicable diseases and not cancer alone

D — hospital admission of every person above forty: Routine admission of everyone is neither possible nor necessary

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Opportunistic screening during any contact with the health system finds many cases early and costs very little
option_3: screening, health promotion and management of non-communicable diseases at the primary level
option_4: hospital admission of every person above forty

question: Immunisation and health education given at the sub-centre and primary health centre belong to the level of care known as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. primary level

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The primary level is the first contact with the health system and includes promotion, prevention and simple curative care

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rehabilitative level: Rehabilitation is usually provided at all levels and is not the term for this first contact

B — secondary level: The secondary level provides referral and specialist inpatient care

D — tertiary level: The tertiary level provides highly specialised services in large institutions

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Most of the disease burden in a community can be dealt with at the primary level if it is properly staffed and supplied

question: Herd immunity means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. enough members of a community are immune to a disease, so its transmission is interrupted and even those who are not immune are protected

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When a high proportion of the population is immune, the organism can no longer find enough susceptible people to pass from one person to another

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the whole community receives an antibiotic at the same time: Mass medication is not the definition of herd immunity

C — the community has no cases of any disease: The absence of all disease is not implied

D — every person in a community has been infected in the past: Past infection in every person is not required, as immunisation has the same effect

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is why a few children who cannot be immunised are still protected when the community coverage is high
option_1: enough members of a community are immune to a disease, so its transmission is interrupted and even those who are not immune are protected
option_2: the whole community receives an antibiotic at the same time
option_3: the community has no cases of any disease
option_4: every person in a community has been infected in the past

question: During a house visit a community nurse finds that a family stores drinking water in an open mud pot and draws it out with a mug kept on the floor. The most useful step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. show the family how to use a covered container with a long handled ladle hung on a stand, and explain why this prevents contamination

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Safe storage with a cover and a dedicated, hanging ladle removes the route by which hands and the floor contaminate the water, and demonstrating it makes the change practical

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ask the family to buy bottled water for the children: Bottled water is unaffordable and does not address the storage problem

C — advise the family simply to boil the water: Boiling helps but the water is re contaminated in the same open pot

D — tell the family that their pot is unhygienic and leave it at that: Pointing out the fault without a solution does not change behaviour

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Household water handling, and not only the source, is a common reason why diarrhoea continues in a village with a safe supply
option_1: show the family how to use a covered container with a long handled ladle hung on a stand, and explain why this prevents contamination
option_2: ask the family to buy bottled water for the children
option_3: advise the family simply to boil the water
option_4: tell the family that their pot is unhygienic and leave it at that

question: Which of the following is regarded as a primary social institution?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the family

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The family is a primary institution, because it is the earliest, most intimate and most enduring group that shapes the individual

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a political party: A political party is also a secondary institution

B — a trade union: A trade union is a secondary institution formed for a specific purpose

D — a hospital: A hospital is a formal organisation and not a primary institution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The family is the main source of care and of health decisions in Indian society, so the nurse works with it rather than around it

question: In a village the nurse finds that several girls have not completed their immunisation while their brothers have. The most appropriate action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. discuss with the family and the village leaders how gender bias is harming the girls' health, and arrange for the girls to be immunised

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gender bias is a social determinant of health, and changing it requires working with the family and the community rather than blaming one household

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — immunise only the boys in future: This would make the injustice worse

C — ignore it because immunisation is voluntary: Ignoring the gap leaves the girls exposed to preventable disease

D — report the family to the police: Police action is unnecessary and would destroy the relationship with the community

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Social determinants such as gender, caste and poverty decide who receives care, so the nurse tracks coverage by sex and by social group
option_2: discuss with the family and the village leaders how gender bias is harming the girls' health, and arrange for the girls to be immunised

question: Social stratification in a community is important to the community health nurse mainly because it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. influences access to health services, health seeking behaviour and health outcomes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Differences of caste, class, education and income shape who can reach a service and who uses it, which is why coverage differs between groups

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — is relevant only in urban areas: It matters in rural areas at least as much as in cities

B — has no relation to health: Stratification is closely linked with health inequality

C — decides the number of health centres to be built: The number of centres depends on population norms and planning

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse collects data separately for disadvantaged groups so that hidden gaps become visible
option_3: decides the number of health centres to be built
option_4: influences access to health services, health seeking behaviour and health outcomes

question: Nursing research is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a systematic and orderly enquiry designed to answer a question and add to knowledge

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Research uses a planned, orderly method to answer a defined question and to produce knowledge that others can examine

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a random collection of opinions about patient care: Opinions without a method are not research

C — a personal study of an interesting case: A single case study is one design within research and only when it is conducted systematically

D — the routine recording of vital signs: Routine recording is practice and not research

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Evidence based nursing depends on research being read, understood and applied at the bedside
option_1: a random collection of opinions about patient care
option_2: a systematic and orderly enquiry designed to answer a question and add to knowledge
option_3: a personal study of an interesting case

question: In a study of the effect of a teaching programme on hand hygiene compliance, the dependent variable is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the hand hygiene compliance

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researcher measures and expects to change, here the compliance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the name of the hospital: The hospital is the setting of the study

C — the number of nurses in the ward: The number of nurses may act as an extraneous variable

D — the teaching programme: The teaching programme is the independent variable, the intervention that is manipulated

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Clearly naming the variables at the start keeps the study focused and makes the results interpretable
option_3: the number of nurses in the ward

question: A hypothesis in a research study is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a tentative statement about the relation between two or more variables that the study sets out to test

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The hypothesis is a testable prediction about how the variables are related, framed before the data are collected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a list of the references used: References support the literature review

B — the name of the statistical test: The choice of statistical test follows from the design and hypothesis

C — the final conclusion of the study: The conclusion is drawn after the analysis is complete

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A study without a clear hypothesis usually produces data that cannot answer any useful question
option_4: a tentative statement about the relation between two or more variables that the study sets out to test

question: Blood groups of a group of patients, such as A, B, AB and O, are an example of which type of data?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. nominal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Nominal data classify subjects into categories that have no order or rank, as with blood groups or sex

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — interval: Interval data have equal distances between values, as with temperature in degrees

C — ordinal: Ordinal data are ordered, as in a pain score of mild, moderate and severe

D — continuous: Continuous data can take any value within a range, as with weight or height

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The type of data decides which statistical test can be used, so it is recorded at the time of data collection

question: Which measure describes how widely the values in a set of observations are spread around the mean?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the standard deviation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The standard deviation expresses the average distance of the values from the mean and is the commonest measure of dispersion

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the total number of observations: The number of observations is the sample size

B — the median: The median is a measure of central tendency

C — the mode: The mode is also a measure of central tendency

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Two wards may have the same mean wait, but the one with the larger standard deviation has far more unpredictable waits

question: A balanced diet is one that provides:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. all the nutrients in the required amounts and proportions along with adequate fibre and water

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A balanced diet supplies energy, protein, fat, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water in the correct proportions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — as many calories as possible: Excess calories cause obesity rather than health

C — only vitamins and minerals: Vitamins and minerals provide no energy and no protein

D — only proteins and fats: Proteins and fats alone would lack vitamins, minerals and fibre

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: A balanced diet is built from locally available cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruit, milk and a small amount of fat rather than from expensive foods
option_2: all the nutrients in the required amounts and proportions along with adequate fibre and water

question: A 26-year-old woman attends the antenatal clinic with a haemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL. She is 14 weeks pregnant and eats very little green leafy vegetable. The most appropriate nursing action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. give her the prescribed iron and folic acid, explain how to take it, advise an iron rich diet and arrange a repeat haemoglobin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Iron and folic acid supplementation with dietary advice and a repeat test is the standard management of anaemia in pregnancy at this level

🔍 Key Clues: 26-year-old | 8.5 g/dL | 14 weeks

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — arrange admission to hospital at once: Admission is needed only for severe anaemia or heart failure

B — reassure her that anaemia is normal in pregnancy: Anaemia in pregnancy is common but it is not normal and it raises the risk of maternal death

D — advise her to stop taking any iron because it causes constipation: Constipation is managed with fluids, fibre and timing rather than by stopping the iron

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron is best absorbed when taken on an empty stomach with a source of vitamin C, and tea with meals reduces absorption
option_2: reassure her that anaemia is normal in pregnancy
option_3: give her the prescribed iron and folic acid, explain how to take it, advise an iron rich diet and arrange a repeat haemoglobin
option_4: advise her to stop taking any iron because it causes constipation

question: Which foods are called protective foods?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. vegetables and fruits

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vegetables and fruits are rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants that protect against deficiency and disease

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — refined oils: Oils are concentrated sources of energy and of fat soluble vitamins

C — sugar and jaggery: Sugar and jaggery provide energy only

D — cereals and millets: Cereals and millets are energy giving foods

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The diet is planned as energy giving, body building and protective foods together, which is easy for a family to remember

question: Under the national programme for control of blindness, vitamin A solution is given to children mainly to prevent:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. xerophthalmia and nutritional blindness

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Periodic vitamin A supplementation prevents xerophthalmia and keratomalacia, which cause preventable blindness in young children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rickets: Rickets is due to deficiency of vitamin D

C — scurvy: Scurvy follows deficiency of vitamin C

D — dental caries: Dental caries are related to oral hygiene and sugar intake and not to vitamin A

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dose is given at the routine immunisation contacts so that coverage is high without extra visits

question: The mid upper arm circumference of a young child is used in the community mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. screen for acute malnutrition quickly without a weighing scale

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mid upper arm circumference changes little during the first years of life and gives a reliable, quick screen for acute malnutrition where weighing is difficult

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — estimate the birth weight: Birth weight is recorded at birth and cannot be estimated from the arm

B — compute the body mass index: The body mass index requires both weight and height

D — measure the child's weight for age: Weight for age is a separate measure and cannot be replaced by the arm circumference

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

C — capital budget: A capital budget relates to large one time items such as buildings and major equipment

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Consumable stock is checked against the patient load, and wastage is a common reason for a ward overspending

question: The normal pH of arterial blood in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 7.35 to 7.45

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Arterial blood is maintained within a narrow range of about 7.35 to 7.45 by buffers, respiration and the kidneys

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 6.8 to 7.0: A pH of 6.8 to 7.0 is incompatible with life

C — 5.0 to 5.5: This range is strongly acidic

D — 7.8 to 8.0: This range is strongly alkaline and would not occur in life

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Even small deviations of pH from this range change the action of drugs and enzymes, so the value is always read with the carbon dioxide and bicarbonate

question: According to Maslow's hierarchy, which need follows the safety needs?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. love and belonging needs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Once the physiological and safety needs are reasonably met, the need for love, affection and belonging assumes priority

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — esteem needs: Esteem needs lie above belongingness

C — self-actualisation: Self-actualisation is at the top of the hierarchy

D — physiological needs: Physiological needs come below the safety needs

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient who feels lonely and unsupported after discharge often fails to follow the treatment plan despite knowing what to do

question: If both parents are carriers of an autosomal recessive disorder, the risk that each child will be affected is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 25 percent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two carriers have one chance in four of having an affected child, one in two of having a carrier child and one in four of having an unaffected child

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 100 percent: A risk of one hundred percent would need both parents to be affected rather than carriers

B — nil: The risk is not nil, and this is why counselling is important

D — 50 percent: Fifty percent is the risk of the child being a carrier

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The distinction between being a carrier and being affected is the first thing that parents need explained

question: When a nurse realises that she has given a wrong dose of a drug, the correct action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. assess the patient, inform the doctor at once, record the incident honestly and complete the incident report

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The priority is the safety of the patient, followed by prompt reporting, honest documentation and the incident report

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — say nothing if the patient seems well: Concealment prevents the patient from being observed for the effect of the error

B — wait until the end of the shift and then tell the nurse in charge: Delaying the report puts the patient at avoidable risk

D — alter the chart to make the record look correct: Altering the record is falsification and is itself misconduct

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The purpose of the incident report is to prevent recurrence, not to punish, and a nurse who reports honestly is protected when she does so promptly
option_1: say nothing if the patient seems well
option_2: wait until the end of the shift and then tell the nurse in charge
option_3: assess the patient, inform the doctor at once, record the incident honestly and complete the incident report
option_4: alter the chart to make the record look correct

question: The National Institute of Nutrition is located in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Hyderabad

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Institute of Nutrition, the country's main nutrition research body, is situated in Hyderabad

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Kolkata: Kolkata has research institutes of its own but not the National Institute of Nutrition

B — Delhi: Delhi is home to the Indian Council of Medical Research, which coordinates this institute

D — Mumbai: Mumbai hosts several national health institutes but not this one

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The institute publishes the dietary guidelines and food composition tables that nurses use for diet planning and patient education

question: The headquarters of the United Nations Children's Fund is located in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. New York

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The headquarters of the United Nations Children's Fund is in New York

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Paris: Paris hosts the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization

C — Rome: Rome hosts the Food and Agriculture Organization

D — Geneva: Geneva hosts the World Health Organization and several other agencies

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The fund supports child health, nutrition and immunisation programmes in India, and its publications are a useful source for community nurses

question: The Indian state with the largest population is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Uttar Pradesh

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state of India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — West Bengal: West Bengal is the fourth

C — Bihar: Bihar is the third most populous state

D — Maharashtra: Maharashtra is the second most populous state

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Population size decides the number of health centres and the staffing norms, which is why the most populous states need the largest health infrastructure

question: Which Indian city is popularly known as the Silicon Valley of India?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Bengaluru

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bengaluru is called the Silicon Valley of India because of its concentration of information technology companies and research institutions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Hyderabad: Hyderabad is known for pharmaceutical and technology industries but not by this name

C — Chennai: Chennai is a major industrial and medical centre

D — Pune: Pune is an industrial and educational centre

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Large cities such as these attract patients from far away, which is one reason why tertiary hospitals in them are so heavily loaded

question: The Green Revolution in India is chiefly associated with a large increase in the production of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. food grains, especially wheat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Green Revolution used high yielding varieties, fertilisers and irrigation to raise the production of food grains, wheat in particular

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cotton: Cotton is a cash crop and is not the focus of this programme

B — milk: A large increase in milk production is called the White Revolution

C — fish: Fish production is not the concern of the Green Revolution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Better food grain availability improved nutrition and reduced famine, which had a direct effect on child survival

question: In terms of area, the Indian state with the largest forest cover is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Madhya Pradesh

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area of any Indian state, though Mizoram has the highest proportion of its area under forest

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Kerala: Kerala has a high proportion of forest but a much smaller total area

B — Punjab: Punjab has one of the smallest forest covers

D — Mizoram: Mizoram leads in percentage of geographical area covered by forest and not in total area

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Forest cover affects rainfall, vector breeding and the availability of medicinal plants, all of which matter to community health

question: The Census of India is conducted by the office of the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India conducts the decennial census and also compiles the civil registration data

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — National Sample Survey Office: The National Sample Survey Office runs sample surveys and not the census

B — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: The health ministry uses census data but does not conduct the census

C — Election Commission of India: The Election Commission conducts elections and uses census data for delimitation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Census figures for population, sex ratio and literacy are the denominator for every rate the community nurse calculates
option_4: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India

question: The India Meteorological Department was established in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1875

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The India Meteorological Department was established in 1875 and provides weather forecasts and cyclone warnings

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1905: 1905 is thirty years later than its establishment

C — 1947: 1947 is the year of independence

D — 1930: 1930 is after the department was founded

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Cyclone and flood warnings from this department are the trigger for pre-positioning relief and medical teams in coastal districts

question: The gas that is essential for combustion is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. oxygen

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Combustion needs oxygen, which combines with the fuel and releases heat and light

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — helium: Helium is an inert gas and does not burn

B — carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide extinguishes a fire by excluding oxygen

C — nitrogen: Nitrogen is inert and does not support combustion

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is why a fire is smothered when oxygen is cut off, and also why oxygen cylinders must be kept away from all flames

question: The atomic number of oxygen is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 8

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Oxygen has eight protons in its nucleus, so its atomic number is eight

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 16: Sixteen is the atomic weight of oxygen and not its atomic number

B — 6: Six is the atomic number of carbon

C — 12: Twelve is the atomic number of magnesium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oxygen makes up about a fifth of the air, and an adequate inspired concentration is essential in every emergency

question: In a green plant, photosynthesis takes place mainly in the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. leaf

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The leaf contains chlorophyll and has a broad flat surface with stomata, which makes it the main organ of photosynthesis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — root: Roots absorb water and minerals but carry out no photosynthesis

C — stem: Green stems can photosynthesise to a small extent only

D — flower: Flowers are concerned with reproduction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is the reason a balanced diet includes green leafy vegetables, which are rich in the products and pigments of photosynthesis

question: The unit of pressure is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pascal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One pascal is a force of one newton acting on an area of one square metre

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — joule: The joule is the unit of energy or work

C — newton: The newton is the unit of force

D — watt: The watt is the unit of power

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Blood pressure is still recorded in millimetres of mercury, but the same idea of force per unit area explains why a small cuff gives a falsely high reading

question: Glycogen is stored mainly in the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. liver

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The liver stores glycogen and releases glucose into the blood to keep the level steady between meals

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — spleen: The spleen stores blood cells and takes part in the immune response

B — kidney: The kidney excretes waste and regulates fluid and electrolytes

D — pancreas: The pancreas secretes insulin, glucagon and digestive enzymes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: This store is why a patient who is fasting can still maintain a normal blood glucose for several hours, and why it fails during prolonged starvation

question: Which blood cells are chiefly responsible for clotting?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. platelets

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Platelets adhere to the injured vessel wall and form the plug on which the clot is built

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — eosinophils: Eosinophils increase in allergy and parasitic infection

C — red blood cells: Red cells carry oxygen

D — lymphocytes: Lymphocytes are part of the immune response

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A low platelet count is watched for closely, as spontaneous bleeding and bruising appear below the usual critical level

question: The number of electrons in the outermost shell of a carbon atom is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 4

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Carbon has four electrons in its outermost shell, which is why it forms four bonds and gives rise to the huge family of organic compounds

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2: Two electrons would allow only two bonds

C — 6: Six is the total number of electrons in a carbon atom and not those in the outer shell

D — 8: Eight outer electrons would make the atom chemically inert, as in neon

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Much of drug chemistry and of human biochemistry rests on the bonding behaviour of carbon

question: The relation between current, voltage and resistance in a conductor is given by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Ohm's law

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage and inversely proportional to the resistance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Faraday's law: Faraday's laws deal with electromagnetic induction

C — Newton's law: Newton's laws describe motion

D — Fleming's rule: Fleming's rules are used to find the direction of a current or of a force in a magnetic field

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The same relation explains why a worn, high resistance lead on an electrical device can overheat and cause a fire

question: What is 15 percent of 200?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 30

🧠 Method: Ten percent of 200 is 20 and five percent is 10, so fifteen percent is 30

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20: 20 is only ten percent

C — 45: 45 is twenty two and a half percent of 200

D — 15: 15 is seven and a half percent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working out a percentage in simple parts is a fast way to check a figure without a calculator

question: The average of 10, 20 and 30 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 20

🧠 Method: The sum is 60 and dividing by 3 gives 20, which is also the middle value

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15: 15 is half of 30 and does not follow from the sum

B — 30: 30 is the largest of the three numbers

D — 25: 25 is above the middle value

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: For an ordered set with an odd number of values the middle value is the average, which makes quick mental checks easy

question: If 8 men can complete a work in 12 days, how many days will 6 men take to complete the same work?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 16 days

🧠 Method: The total work is 96 man days, and dividing by 6 men gives 16 days

⚡ Fast Approach: Combine rates as 1/A + 1/B, then invert to get the number of days.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 9 days: 9 days would be the time taken by more men, not fewer

C — 18 days: 18 days would need only five and a third men

D — 14 days: 14 days does not correspond to a whole number of man days here

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: The same reasoning explains why a reduced nursing team takes longer to complete a fixed set of tasks

question: A car covers 150 kilometres in 3 hours. Its average speed is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 50 kilometres per hour

🧠 Method: Speed is distance divided by time, so 150 divided by 3 gives 50 kilometres per hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the two speeds.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 45 kilometres per hour: 45 would be the speed if the time were 3 hours 20 minutes

C — 60 kilometres per hour: 60 would be the speed if the distance were 180 kilometres

D — 75 kilometres per hour: 75 would be the speed if the time were 2 hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The travelling time to a referral hospital is calculated in this way before a patient is sent, which matters in an emergency

question: The simple interest on 2000 rupees at 5 percent per annum for 4 years is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 400 rupees

🧠 Method: Simple interest is 2000 multiplied by 5 multiplied by 4 and divided by 100, which gives 400 rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: SI = P x R x T / 100. Keep T in years - convert months to a fraction.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 800 rupees: 800 rupees would need twice the rate or period

C — 100 rupees: 100 rupees is the interest for one year

D — 500 rupees: 500 rupees does not correspond to this rate over four years

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Nurses and patients alike should be able to work out the interest on a loan before agreeing to it

question: The price of an article is reduced from 500 rupees to 400 rupees. The percentage decrease is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20 percent

🧠 Method: The decrease is 100 rupees on an original price of 500 rupees, which is one fifth, that is 20 percent

⚡ Fast Approach: Take a base of 100, apply the changes one after another, and compare the final figure with the base.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 80 percent: 80 percent would be a decrease of 400 rupees

C — 25 percent: 25 percent would be a decrease of 125 rupees

D — 10 percent: 10 percent would be a decrease of 50 rupees

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The percentage is always calculated on the original price, and this is a common source of error in interpreting a discount

question: A and B together can finish a work in 12 days, and A alone can finish it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone finish the work?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 30 days

🧠 Method: Together they do one twelfth and A alone one twentieth a day, so B does one twelfth minus one twentieth, which is one thirtieth a day, that is 30 days

⚡ Fast Approach: Combine rates as 1/A + 1/B, then invert to get the number of days.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 8 days: 8 days would be faster than the two working together, which is impossible

B — 32 days: 32 days comes from adding the two times wrongly

D — 24 days: 24 days would make B slower than the actual rate allows

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Common sense is used as a check, since one worker alone can never be faster than the two together

question: Complete the series: Z, X, V, T, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. R

🧠 Method: Each term moves two letters backwards in the alphabet, so after T comes R

⚡ Fast Approach: Number the letters A=1 to Z=26 and work with numbers instead of letters.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — U: U is a letter after T and moves in the wrong direction

C — S: S is only one letter before T

D — Q: Q would skip an extra letter

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Recognising a simple repeating pattern is the same skill used when reading a sequence of sample numbers

question: If A is 1, B is 2 and so on, what is the sum of the letters of the word CAB?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 6

🧠 Method: C is three, A is one and B is two, so the sum is six

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7: Seven would need one letter to be counted twice

B — 8: Eight does not correspond to these letters

C — 5: Five would be the sum of A, A and C

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working carefully letter by letter avoids the slips that matter when transcribing a drug name

question: In a row of 25 students, Ravi is ninth from the left. What is his position from the right?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 17th

🧠 Method: The two positions add up to one more than the total, so 25 plus 1 minus 9 gives 17

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15th: 15 would give a total of 23

B — 18th: 18 would give a total of 26

C — 16th: 16 would mean a total of 24

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Careful counting prevents errors when tallying patients present at the start and end of a shift

question: Find the odd one out: 16, 25, 36, 49, 60.
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 60

🧠 Method: Every number except 60 is a perfect square

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 25: 25 is the square of five

B — 49: 49 is the square of seven

C — 36: 36 is the square of six

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Testing each item against one clear rule is the approach used to spot a wrongly labelled specimen in a batch

question: If P means plus, Q means minus and R means multiplied by, then the value of 8 R 3 Q 4 P 2 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 22

🧠 Method: The expression becomes 8 multiplied by 3 minus 4 plus 2, which is 24 minus 4 plus 2 and so equals 22

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 18: 18 comes from subtracting the last two figures twice

B — 20: 20 comes from ignoring the final addition

C — 26: 26 comes from adding four instead of subtracting it

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Working step by step in the correct order avoids the slips that cause errors in drug calculations

question: All nurses are caring. Some caring persons are men. Which conclusion follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. only the conclusion that some men are caring follows

🧠 Method: The second statement says directly that some caring persons are men, so some men are caring, but nothing links nurses to men

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only the conclusion that some nurses are men follows: The first conclusion does not follow from these statements

B — neither conclusion follows: The second conclusion does follow

D — both conclusions follow: Not both conclusions follow, since the first is unsupported

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Distinguishing what certainly follows from what merely seems likely is central to clinical reasoning
option_1: only the conclusion that some nurses are men follows
option_3: only the conclusion that some men are caring follows

question: The angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 6 o'clock is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 180 degrees

🧠 Method: At six o'clock the hands point in exactly opposite directions, six hour spaces apart, and six multiplied by thirty gives 180 degrees

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 90 degrees: 90 degrees is the angle at three or nine o'clock

C — 120 degrees: 120 degrees is four hour spaces

D — 150 degrees: 150 degrees is five hour spaces

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Accurate reading of the clock prevents errors when recording the time of a dose or of an incident
